restitution_schema.rule: unary restitution per class (the value and range of each class's `restitution` field), with optional per-asset and per-fill overrides: `fill_overrides.full` on a class for a liquid-filled container (empty = the class value; #85). No runtime pair table: PhysX has no pair restitution, it combines the two unary values with the collider's restitution_combine_mode (average here).
restitution_schema.pair_bands: pair bands (PR #84) are load-time check assertions only where the impact speed exceeds the 0.5 m/s bounce threshold (env/environment/base_env.py:27); unary overrides reproduce all 20 of #84's pair bands (Wenhao's side review of #73).

mu_static.basis: Shore A 60–90 silicone/TPU/rubber gripper pad (`pad_elastomer`) pinching smooth or textured ABS/PC device shells (mice, earbuds, keyboards, camera housing). Compliant elastomer drapes over polymer surface roughness and develops adhesive shear above rigid polymer-on-polymer contacts: `0.40` covers dusty or hard-durometer TPU on textured matte ABS, `0.70` represents clean medium-durometer elastomer grip, and `1.20` covers clean soft silicone on glossy PC/ABS (`abs_device_housing__rubber_elastomer` has the same `1.20` ceiling in `class_values.json`).

mu_kinetic.basis: Slip of an ABS/PC device housing under a Shore A 60–90 elastomer finger pad. Viscoelastic hysteresis and interfacial shear during slip keep kinetic friction high (`0.60` nominal) while ~15% below static breakaway; `[0.30, 1.00]` spans dusty hard TPU (`0.30`) to clean high-grip silicone (`1.00`).

mu_static.basis: Hard thermoplastic X5 finger face (`pad_hard`, ABS/PLA analogue) pinching rigid ABS/PC device housings (`sourcing_G1.md` §8 polymer self-pair pad analogue). Matches `abs_device_housing__abs_device_housing` nominal `0.40`, with `[0.25, 0.65]` spanning textured matte ABS/PC shells (`0.25`) to smooth glossy polymer housings (`0.65`).

mu_static.basis: Smooth or satin ABS/PC electronics shells (X5 wrist-camera housing, mice, keyboards, alarm clock, earbuds, tape measure) resting on a dry hard melamine-laminate tabletop (`table_laminate`). Low end `0.15` covers dusty or glossy low-adhesion ABS/PC or PTFE-like mouse feet on hard cured melamine resin; nominal `0.30` sits at typical dry rigid-polymer-on-laminate breakaway; high end `0.50` covers clean textured or matte ABS/PC housings before rubberized feet dominate (`engineered_wood__table_laminate` is `0.30 [0.15, 0.50]` in `class_values.json`).

mu_kinetic.basis: Steady sliding of rigid ABS/PC device shells across dry melamine laminate after breakaway. Kinetic friction of dry unlubricated hard polymers on hard thermoset resin runs ~15–20% below static as micro-asperity junctions shear without ploughing; `[0.12, 0.40]` spans dusty/low-friction polymer glides (`0.12`) to clean matte ABS shells (`0.40`).

mu_static.basis: Rigid ABS/PC device housings resting on a finished/lacquered hardwood tabletop (`table_wood`, simulation shader `Mahogany_Planks.mdl`). Polyurethane or nitrocellulose wood finishes are slightly more compliant and adhesive against rigid thermoplastics than hard melamine resin, shifting `[0.15, 0.50]` upward by `0.05` to `[0.20, 0.55]` (consistent with `abs_device_housing__hardwood` `[0.15, 0.65]` in `class_values.json`).

mu_kinetic.basis: Steady sliding of rigid ABS/PC housings on lacquered wood. Kept ~15% below the static band `[0.20, 0.55]`; `[0.15, 0.45]` spans slick waxed wood lacquer (`0.15`) to clean satin varnish (`0.45`).

mu_static.basis: Moulded ABS/PS/PVC blocks, T-blocks, math/digit tokens, and figurines resting on a dry smooth melamine-laminate tabletop. Both surfaces are hard glassy/semi-gloss polymers with small real contact area: `0.15` covers dusty or glossy injection-moulded PS/ABS on hard melamine, `0.30` is typical dry rigid-plastic breakaway, and `0.50` covers clean satin ABS or plasticized PVC tokens (below `abs_toy_plastic__abs_toy_plastic` ceiling `0.80` because cured melamine thermoset resists polymer ploughing).

mu_static.basis: Moulded ABS/PS/PVC toys and tokens resting on a lacquered/finished wood tabletop. pair_formability.rule: A material pair (m_a, m_b) can form in a task under scenario (pad_class, table_class) iff an episode of that task contains two distinct engine collider bodies b_1 != b_2 carrying m_a and m_b (using asset_id when the asset has material_override, else its assigned material_class) such that at least one of b_1, b_2 is dynamic (Rigid body or robot Articulation link; static Geometry and Scene colliders have RigidBodyAPI disabled/absent and never form static-static contacts in PhysX). It can form a load-bearing contact iff such a body pair exists that is not finger on finger (both bodies gripper finger pads: an empty close, or the grippers of two arms meeting in a handover). Finger-on-finger contact never carries a sliding load these tasks depend on (#167, Bo's side's decision (b)). Any banded pair that cannot form a load-bearing contact in the task (an uncarried class unary, a no_self_contact self-pair, a static-static collider pair, or a finger-on-finger-only pair such as pad_hard__pad_hard) is enforced as a band constraint only and never enters the L2 objective. Across tasks (#59 option 3, #167 decisions 2, 3 and (b)): objective weights come from the committed scripted-solution contact censuses (see PAIR_WEIGHT_RULE): weight 1 iff the pair carries normal load on a non-robot-self body pair in at least one scripted solution, and band-only (weight 0) otherwise.
pair_formability.weight_rule: Presence weighting from the committed scripted-solution contact censuses (#59 option 3, #167 decisions 3 and (b)): a primary-scenario material pair receives weight 1 in the global Stage 1 L2 objective (counted_in_fit_objective = True) iff it can form in at least one task in scope and carries positive normal load (total_normal_impulse_Ns > 0 and actions_force_total > 0 on body pairs that are not robot-link x robot-link) in the committed corrected contact census of at least one task's scripted solution; robot-link x robot-link contacts (finger on finger such as link7|link8 and intra-arm/inter-arm link grazes such as r1.link1|r1.link3) are excluded per #167 decision (b). In Stage 2, each sensitivity-scenario pair (pad_elastomer, table_wood) inherits the presence weight (1 or 0) of its default-scenario counterpart (pad_hard, table_laminate) with Stage 1 classes held fixed. Every weight-0 pair (formable pairs with zero object-contact load in all censused scripts, robot-link x robot-link-only pairs, pairs from tasks without a scripted-solution census yet, and non-formable pairs) is enforced as an exact band constraint only (with 1-hop Fourier-Motzkin cross-band projection in Stages 1-2 and an exact feasible Stage 3 solve for zero-weight classes).
